question: Should OpenClaw add this permanent core plugin permission, durable AI-safety history, and gateway/UI observability surface as one supported product contract?
rationale: The PR is a feature that changes plugin SDK and manifest contracts while adding persistent security-adjacent operator data; code review cannot determine the desired public API, retention, and ownership boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
options.body: Approve a documented minimal event schema, access/privacy boundary, and plugin API, then require the mechanical session-correlation and real-Gateway proof fixes before merge.

options.title: Keep the capability extension-owned
options.body: Decline the new core contract and direct exporters, dashboards, and specialized safety telemetry to plugin surfaces until a concrete missing core API is identified.

options.title: Split the proposal
options.body: Land only independently approved generic seams in a smaller PR and keep durable storage, gateway methods, and UI behind separately reviewed product decisions.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
recommendation.body: Approve a documented minimal event schema, access/privacy boundary, and plugin API, then require the mechanical session-correlation and real-Gateway proof fixes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely routing point for the cross-cutting core product decision; confidence is limited because no direct current-main ownership history was available in the supplied context.
